name: Understand cat behaviour
blurb: Cats are widely misread as aloof when they are actually communicating clearly in a different dialect. Understanding it changes the whole relationship.
steps: Learn the signals: slow blinking as friendly, tail up as a greeting, a twitching tail tip as agitation, flattened ears as fear.
Learn that petting is often overstimulating — most cats prefer cheeks, chin and base of ears, not the belly, and prefer short sessions.
Learn to play correctly: a wand toy moved like prey, hiding and darting, with a catch and a "kill" at the end so the sequence completes.
Learn resource rules: separate food, water and litter in multi-cat homes, and one litter tray per cat plus one.
Learn that vertical space and hiding places reduce stress more than almost anything else you can provide.
Learn that sudden behaviour changes — litter tray avoidance especially — often mean pain, and warrant a vet visit rather than discipline.
tips: Punishment does not work on cats and damages trust. Change the environment instead.
Laser pointers frustrate cats because the hunt never ends. Finish with a physical toy they can catch.
proof: You can read your cat’s mood accurately and it seeks out your company.
